NDT training in Corpus Christi: how it works for Corpus Christi employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training in Corpus Christi follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Your employer's written practice governs certification: you complete classroom training for the method and level, log supervised on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass an annual vision test. Atlantis NDT delivers Level I, II and III training live online or onsite at your Coastal Bend facility, scheduled around turnarounds.

The Coastal Bend is one of the busiest inspection markets in Texas. Refineries along the Corpus Christi Ship Channel, LNG export trains at Portland and Gregory, a world-scale ethane cracker, a crude export port, offshore fabrication yards at Ingleside, pipelines from the Eagle Ford and Permian, a military helicopter overhaul depot and a major bridge programme all generate NDT work at once. When several of those projects peak together, contractors compete hard for certified Level II technicians, and the ones with the right methods and paperwork get the work.

This section goes beyond the overview above: method-by-method course content mapped to Coastal Bend work, the full SNT-TC-1A sequence, delivery that respects turnaround and hurricane-season calendars, the Texas radiographer certification that every RT crew member needs, and Level III support for local NDT companies. For the national overview see our NDT training programmes.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Corpus Christi

Every course is built on the SNT-TC-1A recommended practice and the body of knowledge used by Level III examiners. Individuals join live online cohorts; employers book closed groups delivered at their own facility or yard. Senior technicians can add ASNT Level III exam preparation.

MethodLevelsWhat Corpus Christi employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, IIICorrosion and thickness surveys on refinery piping, vessels and tanks; shear-wave weld examination; dock and marine structure thickness gaugingLevel I: employer requirements only. Level II: Level I training and experience per written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, IIIEncoded weld examination on LNG and petrochemical construction piping, corrosion mapping, pipeline girth weldsConventional UT background normally required
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, IIIThick-wall vessel and heavy piping weld examination and flaw sizing, often paired with PAUT on construction projectsConventional UT background
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, IIIPipe welds in plant construction and turnarounds, pipeline tie-ins, profile RT for corrosion under insulationTexas DSHS radiographer or trainee certification applies in addition to SNT-TC-1A
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, IIIWeld and nozzle inspection, offshore and structural fabrication, lifting equipmentEmployer requirements only for Level I
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, IIIStainless and alloy piping, cryogenic LNG components, aircraft and rotorcraft partsEmployer requirements only for Level I
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, IIIWeld visual inspection, turnaround equipment inspection, structural and bridge surveysVision test and employer requirements
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, IIIHeat-exchanger tube inspection during refinery turnarounds; helicopter component inspection at depot levelEmployer requirements only for Level I; Level II builds on Level I

What this means locally: technicians who want steady Coastal Bend work should build UT and RT to Level II first, then add PAUT and TOFD, which LNG and petrochemical construction projects increasingly specify in place of or alongside RT. ET for heat-exchanger tubing is a strong turnaround specialism. Technicians heading for rotorcraft maintenance should expect aerospace qualification, typically NAS 410, applied by that employer. To plan a sequence, request a Corpus Christi training quote and tell us the work you are targeting.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Corpus Christi, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is an ASNT recommended practice, not a Texas licence. The Texas state certification that exists for radiographers covers radiation safety, not NDT technique. For every method, it is the employer that certifies, under its written practice.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer's written practice defines levels, training, experience, examinations, vision testing and recertification for each method.
  2. Formal classroom training. Documented training for the method and level; minimum hours come from the written practice, normally based on SNT-TC-1A. See the training requirements matrix for reference figures.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised, documented experience in the method. Turnaround and construction work builds experience quickly, provided it is logged properly and signed off.
  4. General examination. A written test on the method's theory and principles.
  5. Specific examination. A written test on your employer's procedures, equipment and the codes you apply, such as ASME Section V techniques with ASME B31.3 or Section VIII acceptance criteria, API 1104 for pipelines, or AWS D1.1 for structures.
  6. Practical examination. Hands-on inspection of real specimens with known flaws, graded under a Level III.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated annually.
  8. Certification. Issued by the employer on the Level III's recommendation, with records kept for owner and Code audits.
  9. Recertification. At the interval in the written practice, and whenever you join a new employer.

On the Gulf Coast, technicians often move between contractors from one turnaround to the next. Keep your own copies of training certificates, exam results and experience logs so each new employer's Level III can credit them quickly. More in our SNT-TC-1A certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Corpus Christi crews

Atlantis NDT does not operate a physical training centre in Corpus Christi or anywhere in the Coastal Bend. Training is delivered in two formats.

Live online. Instructor-led theory for every method and level, joined from home or a site office. It suits technicians on rotations and shift schedules, and employers who cannot release a crew during a busy season. See online NDT training.

Onsite at your facility. Closed-group training at your shop, yard or plant under ASNT Level III oversight, using your equipment, procedures and reference standards. For inspection contractors building a bench of Level II technicians before a big project, this is usually the most efficient route; see corporate NDT training.

Scheduling around turnarounds and the weather. Refinery and petrochemical turnarounds on the Gulf Coast cluster in spring and autumn, and during those windows nobody has spare technicians. The Atlantic hurricane season, from June through November, can also disrupt planned work at coastal sites. Many Corpus Christi contractors therefore use the quieter weeks between turnaround seasons for classroom training and onsite practicals, so newly certified Level IIs are ready for the next peak. Give us your calendar and ask about onsite training for your Corpus Christi crew; cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Corpus Christi

  • Refining. Refineries operated by CITGO, Flint Hills Resources and Valero line the Corpus Christi Ship Channel's Refinery Row. In-service inspection of piping, vessels, tanks and exchangers follows API standards, with UT, RT, ET and increasingly PAUT at Level II in constant demand. Repairs and alterations follow ASME Section VIII and B31.3.
  • LNG export. Cheniere's Corpus Christi Liquefaction facility, including its Stage 3 expansion, is one of the largest construction and operating inspection programmes in the region. Cryogenic stainless and nickel-steel piping needs PT, RT and PAUT, with extensive weld examination during construction.
  • Petrochemicals. Gulf Coast Growth Ventures, the ExxonMobil and SABIC ethane cracker complex near Gregory, and other chemical plants on the Ship Channel generate both construction and maintenance inspection.
  • Crude export and pipelines. The Port of Corpus Christi is the leading US crude oil export gateway, fed by long-haul pipelines from the Permian Basin and the Eagle Ford. Terminal tank inspection, pipeline construction to API 1104, and integrity digs keep UT, RT and PAUT crews busy. Intrastate pipeline safety in Texas is overseen by the Railroad Commission of Texas.
  • Offshore and heavy fabrication. Kiewit Offshore Services at Ingleside builds large offshore platforms and modules, and other yards and fabricators in the area produce modules, vessels and structural steel. MT, UT, RT and VT to AWS D1.1, API and client specifications are routine.
  • Aerospace and military aviation. Corpus Christi Army Depot, located at Naval Air Station Corpus Christi, overhauls and repairs Army helicopters and their engines and components, and Naval Air Station Kingsville trains Navy jet pilots. Depot-level work relies on PT, MT, ET, UT and VT, with personnel qualified under aerospace and military programmes.
  • Bridges and infrastructure. The Harbor Bridge replacement over the Ship Channel is one of the largest bridge projects in Texas, and TxDOT maintains an extensive inventory of coastal steel and concrete structures exposed to salt air, where corrosion and weld inspection are ongoing.
  • Metals. The hot-briquetted-iron plant near Portland and related port industrial facilities use UT, MT and VT for plant maintenance.

Radiography licensing in Texas. Texas is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography is licensed and inspected by the Texas Department of State Health Services Radiation Control Program under 25 TAC §289.255. Individual radiographers must hold Texas industrial radiography certification, which requires completion of an acceptable radiation safety course, supervised experience and a state examination; Texas also accepts certain reciprocal certifications from recognised entities through its reciprocity process. Certification ID cards are time-limited and must be renewed. Radiographer trainees work under the direct supervision of a certified radiographer. SNT-TC-1A RT training covers exposure technique and image interpretation; it does not replace Texas radiation safety certification, and RT crew members need both.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Boilers in Texas fall under the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation's boiler programme, while pressure vessels and piping in refineries and plants are managed under owner mechanical integrity programmes built on API and ASME codes. Local employers most often ask for Level II in UT and RT, a Texas radiographer card for RT crews, PAUT for construction projects, and clean training and experience records. Many also expect API inspector certificates for senior roles, which are separate schemes. For earnings context see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Corpus Christi NDT companies

The Coastal Bend has a steady flow of new and growing inspection contractors formed to serve turnarounds and construction projects. Owners and EPCs audit them before awarding work, and the first question is usually: show us your written practice, your procedures and your Level III.

  • Written practice development. A written practice built around your methods, levels and client codes, with training, experience, examination and vision record forms ready for owner audits. See written practice development.
  • Outside Level III services. Examination preparation and grading, procedure approval and certification sign-off under your written practice, so you can bid on work without a full-time Level III.
  • Procedure and technique review. UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET procedures aligned to ASME Section V, B31.3, Section VIII, API 1104 and your clients' specifications.
  • Pre-project readiness. Structured training for new hires ahead of a turnaround or construction award, delivered onsite.

Book a Level III consultation and we will start with a review of your current documentation. Background reading: SNT-TC-1A guidance.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Corpus Christi trainees, the oil and gas site and storage tank scenes closely resemble refinery, terminal and LNG work, the welding workshop mirrors the Ingleside yards and local fabricators, and the aircraft hangar suits technicians heading for rotorcraft maintenance.

The simulator is practice only. It does not replace the practical examination on real specimens graded under a Level III, and it does not count toward on-the-job experience unless your employer's written practice explicitly says so. Use it for repetition and confidence before the real exam.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He is responsible for course content and examinations, oversees onsite programmes and works with employers on written practices and Level III services.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Corpus Christi

How do I get NDT certified in Corpus Christi?

Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after formal training, documented experience, general, specific and practical examinations under a Level III, and a vision test. If you are new, start with Level I in UT, MT or PT and approach Coastal Bend inspection contractors, fabricators or plant contractors that will certify you under their written practice. RT candidates also need Texas radiographer trainee status.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas?

Yes, theory for every method and level is available as live online instruction. Practical skills and the practical examination require real equipment and specimens, arranged onsite with your employer. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and whether you already hold UT Level I. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience for each level; the training requirements matrix lists reference figures. Busy turnaround seasons can help you accumulate logged experience faster, but it still has to be documented.

Do I need a license for radiography in Texas?

Yes. Companies need a DSHS industrial radiography licence, and individuals need Texas industrial radiographer certification, which involves an acceptable radiation safety course, experience and a state exam, or recognised reciprocal certification. Trainees work under direct supervision of a certified radiographer. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is separate and employer-issued.

What does NDT training cost in Corpus Christi?

We do not publish prices. The quote depends on method, level, group size and whether training is online or onsite at your facility. Quotes are returned within one business day; request your Corpus Christi NDT training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Corpus Christi employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard basis for NDT personnel at Coastal Bend refineries, LNG and petrochemical plants, pipelines and fabrication yards. Military aviation work applies aerospace and military qualification programmes, and some international EPCs also accept schemes such as CSWIP or ISO 9712 for their own personnel; SNT-TC-1A remains the local default.

Which NDT methods are most in demand on the Coastal Bend?

UT and RT at Level II are the core, followed by PAUT and TOFD for construction projects and ET for heat-exchanger tubing during turnarounds. MT, PT and VT support every fabrication and maintenance job.

Can you train our crew before the next turnaround?

Yes. Onsite programmes are scheduled around your turnaround and project calendar, typically in the quieter weeks between seasons, under ASNT Level III oversight. See corporate NDT training.

Does Atlantis offer API 510, 570, 653 or CWI courses in Corpus Christi?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A based only. Many Coastal Bend owners also ask for API inspector certificates or AWS CWI for senior roles; those are separate schemes run by other bodies.

How do I prepare for ASNT Level III from Corpus Christi?

Level III requires substantial experience and passing the ASNT Basic and method examinations or an equivalent employer examination. Our ASNT Level III exam preparation runs live online, and practice material such as our UT Level 2 practice questions helps at every level.

Does my certification transfer if I change contractors?

Not automatically. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer. Your Texas radiographer certification is personal and stays with you, but your NDT method certifications must be re-issued by the new employer, who can credit your documented training and experience.

Is PAUT worth learning for LNG and petrochemical projects?

For technicians with solid conventional UT experience, yes. Construction specifications on large Gulf Coast projects increasingly call for encoded PAUT and TOFD on piping and vessel welds, and technicians qualified in those techniques are in demand when projects peak.
